summary: This note summarizes the path of Nazi Germany from the early 1930s Great Depression to the outbreak of World War II. It covers Adolf Hitler's appointment as Chancellor, the establishment of a totalitarian regime, and a series of territorial expansions in the late 1930s. It ends with the German invasions of Poland, Western Europe and the Soviet Union.
one_line: Overview of Nazi Germany's rise under Adolf Hitler, its territorial expansion, and its entry into World War II.
key_facts: The worldwide Great Depression hit Germany hard in the early 1930s, as unemployment soared and people lost confidence in the government.
Adolf Hitler was appointed Chancellor of Germany in January 1933.
Hitler's Nazi Party quickly established a totalitarian regime.
Nazi Germany made increasingly aggressive territorial demands, threatening war if they were not met.
Remilitarization of the Rhineland came in 1936.
The annexation of Austria in the Anschluss occurred in 1938.
Parts of Czechoslovakia were annexed with the Munich Agreement in 1938.
Further territory of Czechoslovakia was taken in 1939.
Germany initiated World War II in Europe with the invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939.
After forming a pact with the Soviet Union in 1939, Hitler and Stalin divided Eastern Europe.
After a "Phoney War" in spring 1940, the Germans swept Denmark and Norway, the Low Countries, and France.
The German conquests in 1940 gave Germany control of nearly all of Western Europe.
Hitler invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941.
